# Quality referential

This referential defines, for each of the 28 domains, the rules to follow while building and the 162 criteria checked at audit time. It is not legal advice.

<!-- Generated by tools/referential.py from plugins/core/referential. Do not edit by hand. -->

## Scoring

- Each criterion is worth 5 (blocker), 3 (major) or 1 (minor). Pass = 100%, partial = 50%, fail or not checked = 0.
- Domain score = points earned / points possible × 10.
- Two scores, each with its own blockers: **Experience** (Product, Features, UX, Content, Support, Ergonomics and information architecture, UI, AI slop, Responsive, Accessibility, Compatibility, Performance); **Engineering and operations** (Security, Privacy, Data, Compliance, Reliability, Tests, Code, SEO and meta, Scalability, Integrations, Payments, Costs, Infrastructure, Deployment, Monitoring, Backups). Each is the average of its domains weighted by the usage profile (vitrine, webapp, saas, mobile, api).
- A blocker is met or not (no partial). Failed or not checked, it caps the domain score at 3/10 and the score it belongs to at 5.9/10. An engineering blocker does not cap the experience score, and the other way round.
- The overall score (average of every domain) is kept for history; it is capped at 5.9/10 as soon as any blocker is open.
- Key tasks declared in .quality/project.json › flows are played step by step on a phone and a desktop; ergonomics, UX and accessibility are judged on those states, not on the empty screen.
- A domain or criterion whose conditions do not apply to the project is skipped.

## Domains

- **Product and experience** : Product, Features, UX, Content, Support
- **Design and accessibility** : UI, AI slop, Responsive, Accessibility, Compatibility
- **Ergonomics** : Ergonomics and information architecture
- **Security and data** : Security, Privacy, Data, Compliance
- **Reliability and code quality** : Reliability, Tests, Code
- **Performance and visibility** : Performance, SEO and meta, Scalability
- **Integrations, payments and costs** : Integrations, Payments, Costs
- **Operations** : Infrastructure, Deployment, Monitoring, Backups

## Product and experience

### Product (PRD)

Usefulness and promise: who the project serves, what problem it solves, what it promises.

**While building**

- Write the promise in one sentence (for whom, which problem, which outcome) before any code, in .quality/project.json.
- List what the project will not do (out of scope) to avoid useless features.
- Every feature must serve the promise; otherwise it leaves the scope.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PRD-01 | The promise is written in one sentence and up to date | Major | Promise present and consistent in .quality/project.json. (inspection) |
| PRD-02 | The first screen says what the product does and for whom, without jargon | Major | Read the home or entry screen: would a stranger get it in 5 seconds? (inspection) |
| PRD-03 | The main action is obvious and reachable on arrival | Major | One visible primary call to action on the entry screen. (inspection) |
| PRD-04 | Every shipped feature serves the promise | Minor | Compare the feature list with the promise and the out-of-scope list. (inspection) |
| PRD-05 | A success metric is defined and measurable | Minor | One metric (sign-ups, games played, sales…) and where it is measured. (inspection) |

### Features (FEA)

Complete behaviour: every announced feature works end to end.

**While building**

- Write a short spec per feature with acceptance criteria before coding.
- A feature is done only when its full flow has been run, not just compiled.
- No button, link or menu leading to a missing feature.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FEA-01 | No main flow is broken | Blocker | flows.json: each key task played to its expected result on phone and desktop; without declared flows, e2e tests or a manual run, saying so. (auto `flow_run`) |
| FEA-02 | No dead link, inert button or visible 'coming soon' page | Major | Browse the UI and search for empty hrefs, empty onClick handlers, visible TODOs. (inspection) |
| FEA-03 | Every feature has written acceptance criteria that are met | Major | Specs present (docs/specs or tickets) and checked. (inspection) |
| FEA-04 | No dead code or half-wired feature | Minor | Search for unused exports, orphan routes, forgotten feature flags. (inspection) |

### UX (UX)

Smooth flows, explicit empty states and errors.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Every screen that shows data has 4 states: loading, empty, error, filled.
- An empty state explains the situation and offers the next action.
- An error message says what happened and how to recover, without raw technical codes.
- Any action over one second shows feedback; any destructive action asks for confirmation or can be undone.
- Forms keep the input on error and show the error next to the field.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UX-01 | Every data screen handles loading, empty, error and filled | Major | Read each data-loading component; simulate an empty list and a failing API; look at the filled state on the flow screenshots, not only the empty screen. (inspection) |
| UX-02 | Errors are explicit and offer a way out | Major | No bare 'Something went wrong', no raw technical message shown. (inspection) |
| UX-03 | Destructive actions are confirmed or undoable | Major | Delete, cancel, reset: confirmation or undo available. (inspection) |
| UX-04 | Forms validate inline and keep the input | Major | Submit an invalid form: errors next to fields, input kept. (inspection) |
| UX-05 | Visual feedback on any action over one second | Minor | Buttons show loading and are disabled while sending (no double submit). (inspection) |
| UX-06 | Predictable navigation: back button, deep links, helpful 404 | Minor | Test the back button, open an inner URL directly, visit a missing URL. (inspection) |

### Content (CNT)

Clarity, accuracy and spelling of the text.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Write short, concrete sentences in the user's vocabulary, not the code's.
- No filler text (lorem ipsum, 'Your title here') or invented figures in production.
- One tone and one name for each thing across the whole project.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CNT-01 | No filler text or fake content in production | Blocker | Search for lorem ipsum, TODO, 'placeholder', fake testimonials, unsourced figures. (auto `placeholder_scan`) |
| CNT-02 | Correct spelling and grammar in every language | Major | Spell checker on copy and translation files. (auto `spellcheck`) |
| CNT-03 | Displayed information is accurate (prices, delays, features) | Major | Compare the site's claims with actual behaviour and configuration. (inspection) |
| CNT-04 | Consistent terminology and tone everywhere | Minor | Same word for the same thing, consistent level of formality. (inspection) |
| CNT-05 | No missing translation key or untranslated text | Minor | Diff locale files; search for hard-coded strings in components. (inspection) |

### Support (SUP)

Help and problem resolution for users.

**While building**

- Provide a visible contact channel and a stated response time.
- Important error messages give an ID the user can send to support.
- Write an FAQ or help page from questions actually asked.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SUP-01 | A contact channel is reachable from every page | Major | Contact or help link in the footer or menu. (inspection) |
| SUP-02 | Server errors show a reference ID linked to the logs | Minor | Trigger a 500: an ID is shown and found in the logs. (inspection) |
| SUP-03 | Common problems have a self-service fix | Minor | Password reset, resend confirmation email, account deletion possible without contacting support. (inspection) |
| SUP-04 | A help page or FAQ covers frequent questions | Minor | Help page present and relevant. (inspection) |

## Design and accessibility

### UI (UI)

Visual consistency, alignment and interactive states.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Define tokens (colours, type, spacing, radius, shadows) before screens, and use only them.
- One spacing scale (e.g. 4 or 8 px); no arbitrary spacing.
- Every interactive element has its states: rest, hover, visible focus, active, disabled, loading.
- One icon library and at most two font families.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UI-01 | Colours, sizes and spacing go through tokens | Major | Search for hard-coded values (hex, arbitrary px, arbitrary Tailwind classes) in components. (auto `design_token_scan`) |
| UI-02 | All interactive elements have hover, visible focus, active and disabled | Major | Go through buttons, links and fields with keyboard and mouse. (inspection) |
| UI-03 | Consistent alignment and grid, nothing overflowing | Major | Screenshots: equal left and right edges, no clipped text, no horizontal overflow. (inspection) |
| UI-04 | Clear and limited type hierarchy | Minor | At most 2 font families and a defined size scale. (inspection) |
| UI-05 | Components reused rather than duplicated with variations | Minor | Search for buttons, cards, modals implemented several times. (inspection) |
| UI-06 | Dark mode is complete and readable | Minor | No component left light, contrast checked in both themes. (inspection) |

### AI slop (SLP)

Removal of generic content, robotic jargon and useless visuals.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Pick a project-specific visual direction at /kickoff (references, mood, constraints), never a default style.
- No default purple gradient, glass cards everywhere, emoji as icons, generic three-column 'Why choose us' sections.
- Ban hollow wording: 'revolutionary', 'effortless', 'unlock your potential', 'dive into', 'seamless', 'elevate'.
- Every visual shows the real product, a real place or real data; otherwise it is removed.
- Animations serve understanding or feedback, never decoration alone.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SLP-01 | No hollow phrase or AI jargon in the copy | Major | Scan the copy with the pack's FR/EN blacklist; reread headings and taglines. (auto `slop_wording_scan`) |
| SLP-02 | The visual direction is project-specific and documented | Major | DESIGN.md states the choices (mood, colours, type) and they show on screen; compare with default templates (raw shadcn, purple gradient, glass). DESIGN.md existing is not enough; following how the references are organised is checked by ERG-08. (inspection) |
| SLP-03 | No decorative visual without information (generic illustrations, blobs, random icons) | Major | For each image or illustration: what real thing does it show? (inspection) |
| SLP-04 | Sections answer a user question, not a template | Minor | Look for generic blocks: invented testimonials, 'Our values', grids of 3 vague benefits. (inspection) |
| SLP-05 | Animations are useful, subtle and respect prefers-reduced-motion | Minor | List animations and their purpose; test with reduced motion enabled. (inspection) |

### Responsive (RSP)

Adaptation to mobile, tablet and desktop.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Design mobile first, then widen; test at 360, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px.
- Touch targets at least 44 × 44 px; no feature available only on hover.
- Images served at the right size (srcset or the framework's image component).

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RSP-01 | No horizontal scroll or clipped content from 360 to 1440 px | Blocker | Screenshots at the 5 reference widths and scrollWidth check, then at every flow step (horizontal_overflow in flows.json). (auto `viewport_screenshots`) |
| RSP-02 | Touch targets at least 44 × 44 px on mobile | Major | Measure buttons, icon links, checkboxes in mobile view. (inspection) |
| RSP-03 | No hover-only feature | Major | Menus, tooltips and actions reachable by touch. (inspection) |
| RSP-04 | Layout adapted to each format, not just shrunk | Minor | Navigation, tables and grids reorganised on mobile and tablet. (inspection) |
| RSP-05 | Safe areas and on-screen keyboard handled on mobile | Minor | Notch, iOS bottom bar and field hidden by keyboard tested. (inspection) |

### Accessibility (A11Y)

Contrast, keyboard navigation and screen readers (target WCAG 2.2 AA).

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Semantic HTML first: button for actions, a for links, one h1, headings in order.
- Contrast at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for components and large text.
- Everything works by keyboard, with always-visible focus and a logical order.
- Every field has a visible label; every meaningful image has alt text; every icon button has an accessible name.
- Information never relies on colour alone.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A11Y-01 | No critical or serious axe-core violation on main pages and flow states | Blocker | axe-core (via Playwright) on each main page and at every step of the key tasks (flows.json). An empty screen with no violation is not enough to pass. (auto `axe`) |
| A11Y-02 | Main flows fully doable by keyboard, visible focus | Major | Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Esc on each key task, in the filled state (test data loaded); modals trap and restore focus. (inspection) |
| A11Y-03 | Compliant contrast (4.5:1 text, 3:1 components) | Major | Measure on colour tokens and rendered pages, in every theme. (auto `contrast_check`) |
| A11Y-04 | Labels, text alternatives and accessible names present | Major | Fields without labels, images without alt, icon buttons without aria-label. (inspection) |
| A11Y-05 | Structure readable by screen reader (headings, landmarks, announcements) | Minor | VoiceOver or NVDA test; errors and notifications announced (aria-live). (inspection) |
| A11Y-06 | 200% zoom without loss of content, page language declared | Minor | Browser zoom at 200%; lang attribute on html. (inspection) |

### Compatibility (CMP)

Browsers and devices.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- Declare target browsers (browserslist) and stick to them for CSS and JavaScript.
- Check support for a recent API before using it, with a fallback if needed.
- Test iOS Safari as well as Chrome: most mobile bugs show up there.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CMP-01 | Main flows tested on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit | Major | Playwright tests on all three engines. (auto `e2e_cross_browser`) |
| CMP-02 | Target browsers declared and respected | Major | browserslist present; no unsupported API without fallback. (inspection) |
| CMP-03 | Tested on at least one real iPhone and one real Android device | Minor | Main flow run by hand on a real device. (manual) |
| CMP-04 | Works without extensions and with an ad blocker | Minor | Blocked third-party scripts do not break the app. (inspection) |

## Ergonomics

### Ergonomics and information architecture (ERG)

How screens are organised and how much effort each key task takes, measured by playing the tasks on a phone and on a desktop, not only the hygiene of each screen.

_Applies if: The project has a user interface_

**While building**

- List 2 to 5 key tasks at /qp:kickoff (project.json › flows), with their test data, and design the screens from them.
- Past a dozen settings, group them in tabs, steps or collapsible sections; an endlessly scrolling settings page is never the answer.
- The result (preview, total, rendering) stays visible while adjusting; on a phone, preview on top and settings panel below.
- The main action is reachable without scrolling, and under the thumb on a phone (bottom action bar).
- Settings follow the order of the task, one decision at a time, with a recommended option already selected; advanced settings are set apart.
- A theme, template or default never overwrites a user's choice without saying so and offering undo.
- Design the phone and the desktop separately: each gets its own layout, not the same page stretched or shrunk.
- Take from the references named in DESIGN.md their organisation (screen structure, navigation, gestures), not only their colours.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ERG-01 | Key tasks are declared and play to the end on a phone and on a desktop | Major | 2 to 5 flows in project.json › flows, with test data; flows.json: every run completed on both devices. No flows: fail. (auto `flow_run`) |
| ERG-02 | Each task stays within the effort budget: pages to scroll, screens scrolled through, actions | Major | flows.json: over_budget empty for every run, on phone and desktop (budgets in scoring.yaml › flow_budgets or in the flow). Only one device within budget: partial. (auto `flow_run`) |
| ERG-03 | Few settings shown at once; beyond that, tabs, steps or collapsible sections | Major | flows.json: max_controls_rendered under budget at every step; if over, uses_disclosure must be true and the screenshot must show one group open at a time. (auto `flow_run`) |
| ERG-04 | The result stays visible while adjusting | Major | Flows that declare preview: preview_visible_while_adjusting of at least 0.8 on both devices. No result to show in the product: n/a, with the reason. (auto `flow_run`) |
| ERG-05 | The main action is reachable without scrolling, under the thumb on a phone | Major | Flows that declare primary: primary_visible true on both devices and primary_in_thumb_zone true on phone. (auto `flow_run`) |
| ERG-06 | A user's choice is never overwritten silently (theme, template, default value) | Major | Read the code that applies a theme, template or preset; in a flow, make a choice then apply the theme: the choice stays, or a message offers undo. (inspection) |
| ERG-07 | Settings follow the order of the task, one decision at a time, with a recommended option | Major | On the flow screenshots: what the user decides first comes first, a recommended option is preselected (or "choose for me"), advanced settings are set apart. (inspection) |
| ERG-08 | The app follows how the DESIGN.md references are organised, not only their palette | Major | For each reference in DESIGN.md › "What we borrow": the principle (preview + toolbar, tabbed panels, steps…) shows on the screenshots, on phone and desktop. No borrow list: fail. (inspection) |
| ERG-09 | Heuristic review of the key tasks: no critical problem, no open major one | Major | Review by the ergonomist agent (Nielsen's heuristics, Bastien and Scapin's criteria) on the screenshot of every step, phone and desktop separately. One critical: fail; one major: partial. (inspection) |

## Security and data

### Security (SEC)

Secret protection, input validation, permissions, rate limiting and security headers.

**While building**

- No secret in the code, the Git repo or the client bundle; server-side environment variables only.
- Validate every external input server-side with a schema (Zod, Valibot…): body, params, query, headers, webhooks, files.
- Check authorisation on every request, server-side, on the requested resource (not just login).
- Rate-limit login, sign-up, password reset, forms and expensive routes.
- Parameterised database queries or ORM; never string concatenation.
- Headers: CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEC-01 | No secret in the repo, Git history or client bundle | Blocker | gitleaks on history; search for keys in the client build; .env ignored by Git. (auto `secrets_scan`) |
| SEC-02 | Every external input is validated server-side with a schema | Blocker | Read every route, server action, webhook handler and upload. (inspection) |
| SEC-03 | Authorisation checked server-side on every resource (no IDOR) | Blocker | For each protected route: can a user read or change another user's resource by changing the ID? (inspection) |
| SEC-04 | No dependency with a known critical or high vulnerability | Blocker | npm audit, pnpm audit or osv-scanner. (auto `deps_audit`) |
| SEC-05 | Rate limiting on sensitive and expensive routes | Major | Login, sign-up, password reset, forms, calls to paid APIs. (inspection) |
| SEC-06 | Security headers present and CSP without needless unsafe-inline | Major | Request against production or staging; check every header. (auto `headers_check`) |
| SEC-07 | Sessions and passwords handled correctly | Major | HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies; argon2 or bcrypt hashing; invalidation on logout; CSRF protection. (inspection) |
| SEC-08 | No injection: parameterised queries, escaped HTML, no command execution with user input | Major | Search for $queryRaw, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval, exec, child_process with external input. (inspection) |
| SEC-09 | Uploads restricted in type and size, stored outside the executable root | Major | Real type check, maximum size, regenerated file name. (inspection) |
| SEC-10 | Errors do not leak internal details | Minor | No stack trace, SQL query or server path in production responses. (inspection) |
| SEC-11 | In-depth security audit run at every major release | Minor | Dated and tracked report from the security-audit skill (Cloudflare). (inspection) |

### Privacy (PRV)

Collection and handling of personal data (GDPR).

_Applies if: Collects personal data (forms, accounts, analytics)_

**While building**

- Collect only the data the promise needs; every requested field has a reason.
- Keep an up-to-date list of data, purpose, retention period and processors.
- No non-essential cookie or tracker before consent; refusing as easy as accepting.
- Let users export and delete their data.
- Never write personal data into logs.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PRV-01 | No non-essential tracker set before consent | Blocker | Load the page without consenting: list cookies, localStorage and third-party requests. (auto `cookie_scan`) |
| PRV-02 | Accurate and accessible privacy policy | Major | It matches the data actually collected and the processors actually used. (inspection) |
| PRV-03 | Minimal collection: no field or tracker without a purpose | Major | Compare forms and data models with the processing register. (inspection) |
| PRV-04 | Users can delete and export their data | Major | Account deletion that really erases (or anonymises) the linked data. (inspection) |
| PRV-05 | No personal data in logs or error tools | Major | Read log calls and Sentry or equivalent config (scrubbing). (inspection) |
| PRV-06 | Retention periods defined and enforced | Minor | Purge job or documented rule for inactive accounts, logs, backups. (inspection) |

### Data (DAT)

Data integrity and consistency.

_Applies if: Database_

**While building**

- Essential business rules also live in the database: foreign keys, NOT NULL, unique constraints, CHECK.
- Every schema change goes through a versioned migration, reviewed and tested on a copy.
- Operations that change several tables run in a transaction.
- Dates in UTC in the database, amounts as integers (cents) or decimals, never floats.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DAT-01 | Migrations are versioned and the database matches the schema | Blocker | prisma migrate status (or equivalent) shows no drift; no manual changes in production. (inspection) |
| DAT-02 | Integrity constraints in the database (foreign keys, unique, NOT NULL) | Major | Read the schema: declared relations, required fields not nullable, business uniqueness. (inspection) |
| DAT-03 | Multiple writes inside transactions | Major | Search for related write sequences outside a transaction. (inspection) |
| DAT-04 | Amounts and dates stored in safe types | Major | No Float for money; dates in UTC with time zone handled on display. (inspection) |
| DAT-05 | Destructive migrations are reversible or preceded by a backup | Minor | Column or table drop: rollback plan or documented backup. (inspection) |
| DAT-06 | Indexes on filtered and joined columns | Minor | Compare frequent queries with declared indexes. (inspection) |

### Compliance (LEG)

Applicable legal obligations and licences. This referential is not legal advice.

**While building**

- At /kickoff, identify the country, the publisher type (individual, company) and the resulting obligations; the compliance-fr module details France.
- Check the licence of every dependency, font, image and icon before adding it.
- Credit resources that require it in a dedicated file or in the footer.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LEG-01 | The publisher's mandatory notices are present | Blocker | Legal notice or imprint depending on the country (see the country compliance module). (inspection) |
| LEG-02 | Dependency licences compatible with the project's use | Major | license-checker or equivalent; no incompatible or missing GPL/AGPL licence. (auto `license_check`) |
| LEG-03 | Fonts, images, icons and sounds used under a valid licence | Major | Source and licence documented for every third-party asset. (inspection) |
| LEG-04 | Terms of use or sale published and accepted | Major | Terms accessible; timestamped acceptance at sign-up or purchase. (inspection) |
| LEG-05 | Legal accessibility obligations assessed | Minor | Depending on country and activity (e.g. European Accessibility Act for some services): statement if required. (inspection) |
| LEG-06 | Third-party content and trademarks used with permission | Minor | Logos, excerpts, content APIs: terms of use respected. (inspection) |

## Reliability and code quality

### Reliability (REL)

Errors, interruptions and edge cases.

**While building**

- Every network call has a timeout, error handling and, if idempotent, limited retries.
- Plan edge cases in the spec: empty list, very long list, special characters, double click, expired session, network loss.
- An error in one component does not take down the whole page (error boundary or equivalent).
- The server shuts down cleanly: it finishes in-flight requests and closes its connections.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| REL-01 | No unhandled error that crashes the server or the app | Blocker | Search for promises without catch, handlers without try/catch, missing error boundaries. (inspection) |
| REL-02 | Timeouts and failure handling on all external calls | Major | fetch, HTTP clients, database, Redis: timeout and failure behaviour. (inspection) |
| REL-03 | Double submit and concurrent requests without side effects | Major | Double click on payment, sign-up, create: a single result (idempotency or lock). (inspection) |
| REL-04 | Correct behaviour offline, on slow network and after session expiry | Major | Cut the network, throttle, expire the session mid-flow. (inspection) |
| REL-05 | Extreme inputs handled (empty, very long, emoji, special characters) | Minor | Enter these values in each field and check display and storage. (inspection) |
| REL-06 | Clean server shutdown (SIGTERM handled) | Minor | Read the entry point: closing of the HTTP server, sockets and connections. (inspection) |

### Tests (TST)

Validation and regression prevention.

**While building**

- Any logic with a branch, loop, money calculation, parsing or security comes with at least one test.
- Every fixed bug gets a test that would have caught it.
- Main flows have an end-to-end test that runs in CI.
- Never declare a task done without running the tests and reading their output.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TST-01 | The test suite passes entirely | Blocker | Run the project's test command; no test skipped without a written reason. (auto `test_run`) |
| TST-02 | Risky logic is tested (money, permissions, calculations, parsing) | Major | List these functions and check a test covers them. (inspection) |
| TST-03 | Main flows have an end-to-end test | Major | Playwright (or Detox, Maestro on mobile) tests for each main flow. (auto `e2e`) |
| TST-04 | Tests run automatically before every production release | Major | CI pipeline that blocks deployment when a test fails. (inspection) |
| TST-05 | Tests check behaviour, not implementation | Minor | No tests that merely mirror the code or mock everything. (inspection) |

### Code (COD)

Maintainability, typing, linting, no console errors and no leftover debug logs.

**While building**

- The simplest code that fully solves the problem: no unrequested abstraction, option or configuration.
- Reuse what exists in the project before adding a dependency or a helper.
- Change only what the task requires; flag the rest instead of rewriting it.
- Strict typing, no unjustified any; automatic lint and format before each commit.
- No debug console.log, commented-out code or temporary file left behind.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COD-01 | No type or build error | Blocker | The stack module's typecheck and build commands. (auto `typecheck`) |
| COD-02 | No lint error | Major | The stack module's lint command. (auto `lint`) |
| COD-03 | No error or warning in the browser console | Major | Open each main page with Playwright and collect the console. (auto `console_check`) |
| COD-04 | No debug log, commented-out code or temporary file | Major | Search for console.log, debugger, large commented blocks, *.bak, *.tmp files. (auto `debug_leftovers_scan`) |
| COD-05 | Strict typing and justified any | Minor | strict enabled; every any or ts-ignore has an explaining comment. (inspection) |
| COD-06 | No over-engineering or duplication | Minor | Single-use abstractions, unused options, copy-pasted functions. (inspection) |
| COD-07 | Up-to-date README: install, run, environment variables | Minor | Follow the README on a clean machine; complete .env.example. (inspection) |

## Performance and visibility

### Performance (PRF)

Asset compression, query optimisation and speed.

**While building**

- Set a budget from the start: LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1 on mobile.
- Images in AVIF or WebP, sized, lazy-loaded below the fold, with reserved dimensions.
- Self-hosted fonts, useful subset, font-display: swap.
- No query in a loop (N+1); paginate every list that can grow.
- gzip or brotli compression and HTTP caching on static assets.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PRF-01 | Core Web Vitals within budget on mobile (LCP, INP, CLS) | Major | Lighthouse mobile on main pages; field data if available. (auto `lighthouse`) |
| PRF-02 | No N+1 query or unpaginated list | Major | Read data access inside loops; log the queries of one page. (inspection) |
| PRF-03 | Images optimised, sized and lazy-loaded | Major | Modern formats, srcset or image component, width and height present. (inspection) |
| PRF-04 | JavaScript shipped to the client within budget | Minor | Bundle analysis; heavy dependencies replaced or loaded on demand. (auto `bundle_size`) |
| PRF-05 | Compression and HTTP caching active on static assets | Minor | content-encoding and cache-control headers on JS, CSS, images, fonts. (auto `headers_check`) |
| PRF-06 | API response time measured and reasonable | Minor | p95 of main routes under 500 ms under normal load. (inspection) |

### SEO and meta (SEO)

Search ranking, indexing, metadata, OpenGraph and favicons.

_Applies if: Public pages meant to be found on the web_

**While building**

- Every public page has a unique title and description, a readable URL and a canonical tag.
- Important content is in the served HTML (server or static rendering), not only client-generated.
- Provide sitemap.xml, robots.txt, OpenGraph, Twitter Card, favicons and manifest.
- Private and staging pages are not indexable.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEO-01 | Public pages are indexable and staging is not | Blocker | No accidental noindex in production; noindex or password on staging. (auto `seo_scan`) |
| SEO-02 | Unique title, description and canonical on every public page | Major | Crawl the site and detect duplicates and gaps. (auto `seo_scan`) |
| SEO-03 | Complete OpenGraph and Twitter Card with a dedicated image | Major | og:title, og:description, og:image (1200 × 630), og:url; preview tested. (auto `seo_scan`) |
| SEO-04 | Main content present in the served HTML | Major | curl the page: main text is in the response. (inspection) |
| SEO-05 | sitemap.xml, robots.txt, favicons and manifest present and valid | Minor | Fetch each file; favicons in several sizes and apple-touch-icon. (auto `seo_scan`) |
| SEO-06 | Structured data suited to the site type | Minor | JSON-LD Organization, LocalBusiness, Product or Article as relevant, validated. (inspection) |
| SEO-07 | Correct hreflang tags for language versions | Minor | Each version points to the others and to itself. (inspection) |

### Scalability (SCL)

Holding up under load.

_Applies if: The project has a server or API_

**While building**

- Estimate expected load (concurrent users, peaks) at /kickoff and size for it, without oversizing.
- Stateless server in local memory: sessions, queues and locks in Redis or the database, so several instances can run.
- Long tasks go through a queue, not the HTTP request.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SCL-01 | Load test at expected load without errors | Major | k6 or autocannon on main routes; error rate and p95 recorded. (auto `load_test`) |
| SCL-02 | No critical state kept only in one instance's memory | Major | Sessions, real-time rooms, counters: stored or synced outside the process (Redis adapter for Socket.io). (inspection) |
| SCL-03 | Long tasks processed in the background | Minor | Email sending, file processing, exports: job queue. (inspection) |
| SCL-04 | Database connection pool sized | Minor | Pool size consistent with instance count and database limit. (inspection) |

## Integrations, payments and costs

### Integrations (INT)

APIs, emails and external services.

_Applies if: Calls to external APIs or services_

**While building**

- Isolate each external service behind a single module: one place to change if the service changes.
- Validate external API responses like user input.
- Verify every webhook signature and process each event only once (idempotency).
- Emails: authenticated domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), text version, unsubscribe link for marketing.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INT-01 | Webhook signatures verified | Blocker | Each handler verifies the signature against the raw body before any processing. (inspection) |
| INT-02 | Webhook events processed only once | Major | Event ID stored; a replay creates no duplicate. (inspection) |
| INT-03 | External responses validated and service outages handled | Major | Schema on responses; degraded behaviour when the service is down. (inspection) |
| INT-04 | Emails authenticated (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and not flagged as spam | Major | DNS records checked; test send to Gmail and Outlook. (auto `email_auth_check`) |
| INT-05 | Each external service isolated in a dedicated module | Minor | No direct SDK calls scattered across the code. (inspection) |
| INT-06 | API quotas and terms of use respected | Minor | Known limits, response caching, required attribution shown. (inspection) |

### Payments (PAY)

Billing, subscriptions and cancellation.

_Applies if: Payments or subscriptions_

**While building**

- Use a hosted payment page (Stripe Checkout or equivalent): no card data goes through our servers.
- Payment or subscription state comes from the provider's webhook, never from the browser redirect.
- The displayed and charged price comes from the server or provider, never from a client-sent value.
- Cancelling is as simple as subscribing and reachable from the account.
- Test in test mode: success, decline, 3-D Secure, renewal failure, refund.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PAY-01 | Access is granted only after confirmation by a signed webhook | Blocker | No access unlocked on the return page or through a URL parameter. (inspection) |
| PAY-02 | The amount cannot be changed by the client | Blocker | Prices are read server-side (price IDs), never taken from the request. (inspection) |
| PAY-03 | Self-service cancellation, as simple as subscribing | Major | Cancellation flow from the account, no mandatory contact. (inspection) |
| PAY-04 | Payment failures and renewals handled | Major | Declined card, 3-D Secure, renewal failure: consistent access and emails. (inspection) |
| PAY-05 | Compliant invoices issued and accessible | Major | Invoices with the mentions required by the country, downloadable by the customer. (inspection) |
| PAY-06 | Price, taxes, commitment and renewal shown before payment | Minor | Clear summary before confirming. (inspection) |

### Costs (CST)

Spending control.

**While building**

- Keep the list of paid services with their monthly cost and what drives it up.
- Spending cap or alert on every usage-billed service (AI APIs, email sending, storage, bandwidth).
- Any user-triggered call to a paid service is authenticated and rate-limited.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CST-01 | Spending caps or alerts on usage-billed services | Major | Budget or alert configured at each provider. (inspection) |
| CST-02 | No public route that triggers an unlimited cost | Major | Routes to paid APIs: authentication, rate limiting, caching. (inspection) |
| CST-03 | Up-to-date cost inventory | Minor | File listing services, cost, billing basis, renewal date. (inspection) |
| CST-04 | Unused resources removed | Minor | Servers, databases, domains, subscriptions with no use. (inspection) |

## Operations

### Infrastructure (INF)

Server configuration, process management and automatic restart.

_Applies if: Hosted on a team-managed server (VPS, dedicated)_

**While building**

- Server configuration described in versioned files (Docker Compose, Nginx config, PM2 ecosystem), never only by hand.
- Every process restarts automatically after a crash and on server reboot.
- Firewall on: only required ports open; database and Redis not exposed publicly.
- SSH by key only, automatic security updates.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INF-01 | Database, Redis and admin ports not publicly exposed | Blocker | External port scan; bindings on 127.0.0.1 or internal Docker network. (auto `port_scan`) |
| INF-02 | Automatic restart after crash and after reboot | Major | restart: unless-stopped, pm2 startup and pm2 save, or a systemd unit. (inspection) |
| INF-03 | Server configuration versioned and reproducible | Major | Rebuild the environment from the repo and a .env. (inspection) |
| INF-04 | HTTPS everywhere with automatic certificate renewal | Major | HTTP to HTTPS redirect; expiry date and auto-renewal. (inspection) |
| INF-05 | Hardened server access (SSH keys, firewall, automatic updates) | Minor | PasswordAuthentication no, ufw or equivalent, unattended-upgrades. (inspection) |
| INF-06 | Resource limits and log rotation | Minor | Memory limit per container or process; logs that do not fill the disk. (inspection) |

### Deployment (DEP)

Release and rollback.

**While building**

- Deploy through one command or pipeline, never by copying files by hand.
- Every deployed version is identifiable (Git tag, build number) and the previous one stays available.
- Write and test the rollback procedure before you need it.
- Deploy to staging first when the change touches data, payments or authentication.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DEP-01 | A rollback procedure exists and has been tested | Blocker | Rollback document and date of last trial. (inspection) |
| DEP-02 | Automated and reproducible deployment | Major | Single script or pipeline; no undocumented manual step. (inspection) |
| DEP-03 | Tests and build gate production releases | Major | The pipeline stops if typecheck, lint, tests or build fail. (inspection) |
| DEP-04 | Migrations applied safely at deployment | Major | Migration and code order compatible; backup before destructive migration. (inspection) |
| DEP-05 | Deployed version identifiable and visible | Minor | Git tag or hash exposed in a health endpoint or the logs. (inspection) |
| DEP-06 | Staging environment separate from production | Minor | Separate database, secrets and domain. (inspection) |

### Monitoring (MON)

Monitoring, error logs and alerts.

_Applies if: The project has a server or API or Public pages meant to be found on the web_

**While building**

- Send server and client errors to a tool (Sentry, GlitchTip…) with the version and no personal data.
- Expose a health endpoint and monitor it from outside (Uptime Kuma, Better Stack…).
- Structured logs (JSON) with a level and a request ID.
- An alert must reach a channel that is read (email, phone), and only for what needs action.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MON-01 | A site outage triggers an alert someone receives | Blocker | External monitoring configured; test alert received. (inspection) |
| MON-02 | Server and client errors reported to a tracking tool | Major | SDK configured, test error visible with version and trace. (inspection) |
| MON-03 | Health endpoint that checks critical dependencies | Major | /health responds and checks database and Redis. (inspection) |
| MON-04 | Structured, timestamped logs kept for a defined period | Minor | JSON format, level, request ID, rotation. (inspection) |
| MON-05 | Alert before domain and certificate expiry, and on disk space | Minor | Monitoring of expiry dates and disk. (inspection) |

### Backups (BAK)

Automated backups, tested restore and recovery.

_Applies if: Database or User file uploads_

**While building**

- Automatic daily backup of the database and user-uploaded files.
- 3-2-1 rule: at least one copy off the production server, with another provider or region.
- Backups encrypted and kept for a defined period.
- Test a full restore at least once a quarter and record how long it takes.

**Audit criteria**

| ID | Criterion | Severity | How to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BAK-01 | Automatic backup of the database and user files | Blocker | Scheduled job and latest backup less than 24 h old. (inspection) |
| BAK-02 | A full restore has been tested | Blocker | Date and duration of the last successful restore on a separate environment. (manual) |
| BAK-03 | At least one copy off the production server | Major | External destination (object storage, other server) checked. (inspection) |
| BAK-04 | Backup failure raises an alert | Major | The backup script alerts on failure or absence. (inspection) |
| BAK-05 | Encrypted backups with a defined retention period | Minor | Encryption and rotation configured. (inspection) |
| BAK-06 | Written recovery plan (who does what, in which order) | Minor | Recovery document with acceptable downtime and data-loss targets. (inspection) |
